```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "B carries a hard regulatory gate before its first sale. It handles PHI, so it needs signed BAAs, a documented risk assessment and audited infrastructure from day one. A sourced estimate puts year-one HIPAA compliance at $8,000-$25,000, which is hard to fit into a one-person, 90-day path to a paying customer. A has no comparable legal barrier.",
    "A's sourced demand evidence shows buyers already paying for trigger-based welcome swag. Hampton runs a production Stripe/Zapier-to-SwagUp workflow, and BurnRate sought a new-customer welcome kit. B's sourced demand evidence is only price complaints about incumbents, and B's own brief says none of them describe a missing notes-plus-reminders product.",
    "A can plausibly reach a first paid pilot faster. A solo operator can put a Stripe webhook wrapper on existing fulfillment platforms and outsource warehousing and printing. B needs a secure, compliant EHR-grade system before any therapist can legally put client data in it.",
    "Both face entrenched incumbents: SwagUp, Sendoso and Z-Swag for A; SimplePractice, TherapyNotes and GReminders for B. Neither brief shows a strong wedge, so competition does not separate them. Regulatory risk and time to first revenue decide it in A's favor."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's core demand thesis is that price-sensitive solo therapists would switch to a stripped-down notes-plus-reminders app. That thesis is inference, not evidence. The Reddit and Oasys quotes show only resentment of SimplePractice pricing, and B's own brief concedes that switching interest flows 'toward other full EHRs, not toward stripped-down tools.' Two of B's competitor prices also have no source (TheraSoft $69/mo, TheraFocus $199/mo), and neither does the claimed SimplePractice $29 tier, so all three count as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A has serious unresolved weaknesses. The Stripe-trigger mechanic is already an existing feature of well-capitalized incumbents, so A risks being a thin reseller layer. Its unit economics at low volume are unproven, with kit costs of roughly $60-$220 against low-ACV SaaS signups. International customs and returns handling could overwhelm a solo operator. A wins mainly because B's HIPAA burden is a more concrete and immediate blocker to a paying customer within 90 days, not because A shows a clearly defensible opportunity."
}
```
